findings.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:1 — no unique index or uniqueness validation on `host` lets two EmbeddableHost rows map the same hostname to two different categories, making `record_for_host`'s `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` return whichever row the DB happens to order first, so a topic embedded from that host silently lands in a non-deterministic category depending on row insertion/scan order (confidence 90, severity P2).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` combined with the one-time backfill of admin-set hosts and the `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts','embed_category')` in the same migration means any later re-run of this migration (e.g. `db:migrate:redo`, a rebuilt multisite schema, or a rollback-then-reapply) drops and recreates the table and re-attempts the backfill from site_settings rows that have already been deleted, permanently losing every admin-configured host/category mapping with no recovery path (confidence 70, severity P2).

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — this file (named for `category`) now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host) do ... end`, while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1 contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators, so the fabricator filenames no longer match their contents and any future test author who greps `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` expecting the embeddable-host fabricator, or edits `category_fabricator.rb` expecting to change category defaults, will edit or read the wrong file (confidence 100, severity P2).

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:22 — the "default to uncategorized if category_id blank" business rule (`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`) lives only in the controller, not on the `EmbeddableHost` model, so any other creation path (rails console, a rake task, a future API endpoint, or direct `EmbeddableHost.create`) bypasses this safety net and hits the DB's `category_id NOT NULL` constraint instead of getting a sensible default, making the model an incomplete owner of its own required-field invariant (confidence 75, severity P3).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 — `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` runs against a plain (non-functional, non-indexed) `host` column, so every embed lookup does a case-insensitive full table scan instead of using an index, which was previously unnecessary because `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` was held in memory rather than queried per embed (confidence 55, severity P3).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:1-33 — the migration that converts existing `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` site_settings rows into `embeddable_hosts` table rows (splitting multi-line hosts, resolving category_id by name-match with uncategorized fallback) has zero test coverage anywhere in the diff, so a regression in the upgrade path for existing installs (the primary reason this migration exists) would go undetected.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:1-9 — the spec for the new admin CRUD controller only asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`; it never exercises `create`, `update`, or `destroy`, so the actual "editable in admin" feature named in the task title has no verification that saving a host/category mapping, editing it, or deleting it works or rejects invalid input.

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:1-9 — same gap as the embeddable_hosts controller spec: only checks subclassing, never calls `show`/`update`, so the admin embedding index page's serialization of `EmbeddableHost.all` is unverified.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:8 — `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` unconditionally drops and recreates the embeddable_hosts table on every re-run, silently destroying any rows already inserted by a prior partial/successful run of this same migration (confidence 90, severity P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:14 — `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes into the SELECT result before checking it is non-nil, so when no category name matches the `embed_category` site_setting value the query returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration outright (confidence 90, severity P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:20 — same crash pattern as line 14: if the `uncategorized_category_id` site_setting row is missing, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['value']` raises NoMethodError, aborting mid-migration after the table has already been created/force-dropped, leaving the database in a half-migrated state (confidence 85, severity P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24 — `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` guards the INSERT backfill loop, but the unconditional `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` at line 36 runs regardless of whether the guard was true, so if `embeddable_hosts` site_setting is absent or empty the settings are still deleted with no corresponding host rows ever created — a backfill-then-delete pattern where the delete is not actually gated on successful backfill (confidence 85, severity P0).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:30 — raw string interpolation of `h` into `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` with no escaping means any host value containing a single quote (a plausible/valid hostname component in stored legacy data, e.g. an apostrophe-laden value) produces malformed SQL that raises and aborts the migration partway through the backfill loop, leaving some hosts migrated and others silently lost before the trailing DELETE still executes (confidence 80, severity P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:36 — the migration uses `change` with only forward `execute` calls and no `down`/`reversible` block; Rails cannot auto-invert `execute`, so this migration is irreversible, and the `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` permanently discards the original settings values with no code path to restore them on rollback (confidence 95, severity P1).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` indexes row 0 of a PG::Result with no bounds/blank check; on any install where `embed_category` was never customized (the common case, since it has no matching site_settings row), the query returns zero rows and `[0]` raises (PG::Result index out of range / NoMethodError on nil), crashing the migration before it can even reach the fallback branch. Confidence 90, Severity P0.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 — `category_id = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` has the identical unguarded `[0]` indexing problem as line 11; `uncategorized_category_id` is a hidden setting with default `-1` (config/site_settings.yml) that is never written to the `site_settings` table unless explicitly overridden, so on a fresh database (e.g. `rake db:test:prepare`, a new install, or CI) this query also returns zero rows and the migration raises instead of falling back to the intended default, meaning the migration cannot successfully run on a stock database. Confidence 85, Severity P0.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:26 — `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` builds the INSERT by interpolating the site-setting-derived host string directly into the SQL literal with no escaping/quoting; any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value containing a single quote (e.g. an admin-entered value like `o'brien.com`) produces malformed SQL and aborts the migration/backfill instead of migrating the data. Confidence 70, Severity P1.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47-53 — `actions.delete()` calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); })` with no `.catch()`, so a failed destroyRecord (server error or network failure) is an unhandled promise rejection: the row is not removed from the admin list, no error is shown to the user, and the bootbox confirm dialog has already closed as if the delete succeeded. app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5-6 — `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with no `.then`/`.catch` and discards the returned promise entirely, so if the PUT request fails the admin sees no error and has no indication the settings were not saved. app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11 — `record_for_host` does `uri = URI(host) rescue nil`, silently swallowing every exception class (not just URI::InvalidURIError) from malformed referer headers with no logging, masking any unexpected parsing failure as an ordinary "host not allowed" case. app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 and lib/topic_retriever.rb:16 — both call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which now runs an uncached `EmbeddableHost.where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` DB query on every public embed request and every topic-retrieval invalid_host? check, replacing the prior `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`/`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` check that read from SiteSetting's in-memory/cached settings, adding a synchronous DB round-trip to a public, unauthenticated request path. spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1-4 — the pre-existing `category`, `diff_category`, `happy_category`, and `private_category` fabricators (unrelated to the embeddable-host feature) were relocated wholesale into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, while `category_fabricator.rb` was gutted to hold only the new `embeddable_host` fabricator, so the file names no longer describe their contents (confidence 75, severity P2).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:191 — the `_hydrateEmbedded` regex was widened from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with a new plural-array hydration branch (lines 199-203), but no code added in this diff (embeddable_host_serializer.rb uses only singular `category_id`, embeddable-host.js.es6 only reads `host.category.id`) exercises the `_ids` plural path, so this is an unexercised, out-of-scope generalization of a shared core model method rather than something required by "edit category/host relationships for embedding" (confidence 75, severity P2).

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` interpolates `h` (a line from the pre-existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` value, itself sourced from raw DB text read at line 20 via `execute(...)[0]['value']`) directly into a SQL string with no escaping/quoting, so any stored value containing a single quote (e.g. `evil.com'); DROP TABLE users;--`) breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary SQL when this migration runs; genuine SQL-injection pattern, though the trigger requires the `embeddable_hosts` setting to already contain attacker-controlled text before the migration runs (normally only settable by a site admin via the old settings UI, or by anyone with direct DB write access) — confidence 90, severity P2 (real injection primitive, but the practical actor who can seed the value already has admin/DB-level trust).

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7 — only asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`; the controller's `create`/`update`/`destroy` actions, the `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` defaulting branch, and `render_json_error` failure path (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb) are entirely unexercised, giving false confidence of coverage for a controller with real logic. spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7 — only asserts the subclass relationship; `show`/`update` actions and `fetch_embedding` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb) are never invoked or asserted on, so the spec is a stale shell providing no behavioral coverage. app/models/embeddable_host.rb:1-24 — new `EmbeddableHost` model (host format regex validation, `before_validation` URL-scheme/path stripping, `record_for_host` URI parsing with rescue-to-nil, `host_allowed?`) has no corresponding spec file anywhere in the repo (no spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb), so none of its validation edge cases, the rescue branch in `record_for_host`, or case-insensitive host matching are directly unit-tested; only indirect coverage exists via embed_controller_spec.rb's happy-path referer checks. app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-40 — the behavior change from `category: SiteSetting.embed_category` to `category: eh.try(:category_id)` has no test anywhere asserting a newly created topic actually receives the matched EmbeddableHost's category_id, nor a test for the nil-category fallback when no host matches; no spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb exists and embed_controller_spec.rb never inspects the created topic's category. app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:1-63 — new Ember component with edit/save/delete/cancel actions using a buffered-content pattern and a `cantSave` computed guard has no corresponding JS test added in this diff, leaving the client-side save/cancel/delete/category-selection logic completely unverified. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with `record_for_host` doing `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) and uses its `category_id` to choose the embed topic category (`TopicEmbed.import` now sets `category: eh.try(:category_id)`). The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` has no unique index on `host`, and the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive). Therefore two rows can exist for the same hostname with different categories, making `.first` dependent on DB scan/insertion order and leading to nondeterministic category selection for embeds from that host.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` does use `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` and later deletes the legacy settings via `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. This does mean that if the migration were ever re-applied against a schema that already had `embeddable_hosts` data (e.g., a nonstandard/manual re-run where the versioning guard is bypassed), `force: true` would drop/recreate the table and the backfill would not be able to repopulate from `site_settings` because those rows are deleted in the same migration. However, under normal Rails migration workflows the migration is not re-run without an explicit rollback/redo (which already drops the table), so the finding’s “any later re-run” framing is overstated as a guaranteed defect in typical operation.
